fact: Mauritius's report to the UN disability committee says Section 23 of the Copyright Act 2014 permits reproduction of published works in accessible format for people with visual impairment and the print disabled, incorporating the Marrakesh Treaty provisions.

The Government of Mauritius says its Ministry of Social Integration set up a disability website, disability.govmu.org, where persons with disabilities can apply online for ministry services, with special features for persons with visual impairment.

The UN Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities says Mauritius's Protection and Promotion of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2024 does not cover the right to information in an accessible format, with only limited measures to promote accessible printed and electronic information, and recommends that it establish accessibility standards for information, communication technologies and websites.

fact: The Mauritian Sign Language electronic dictionary (MSL E-Dictionary) was launched at the Beau-Bassin school for the deaf at a ceremony with social integration minister Ashok Subron, who praised his ministry's collaboration with the Society for the Welfare of the Deaf.
The AI Unit of the Ministry of ICT and Innovation says its website is working to meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA and is not yet fully there.

The AI Unit's government website offers built-in accessibility tools including read-aloud, text scaling from 80% to 200%, high contrast, a dyslexia-friendly font, keyboard navigation and a simple language mode.
The AI Unit states it fixed all critical issues found in its May 2026 accessibility audit of its website, and that some Framework Library PDFs may still not read correctly in a screen reader.
The ICT ministry's Digital Service Framework, first released in August 2026, says ministries must adhere to it and that all digital services must comply with WCAG 2.1 Level AA.
